objective.text: Recognize sub-minute schedules require schedule:run to remain alive for the current minute.

difficulty.rationale: Account for the command remaining active to service repeated events within the current minute.

runtime.sapi: Isolated CLI Laravel harness unless another context is explicitly stated
runtime.errorPolicy: E_ALL; UTC; no external services or application data

stem: An application adds an everyTenSeconds task. Under the normal sub-minute scheduler behavior, why does schedule:run no longer return immediately after its first set of due events?

options.text: It remains active for the rest of the current minute to evaluate repeatable events.
options.rationale: Sub-minute scheduling uses the current command process to service repeat intervals until the minute ends.

options.text: It waits for ten separate cron invocations before starting the task.
options.rationale: The repeated cadence is handled within the minute rather than requiring multiple external cron entries.
options.misconception: The repeated cadence is handled within the minute rather than requiring multiple external cron entries.

options.text: It becomes a permanent daemon and never exits until the next deployment.
options.rationale: The normal schedule:run loop is bounded by the current minute, unlike an indefinitely running service.
options.misconception: The normal schedule:run loop is bounded by the current minute, unlike an indefinitely running service.

options.text: It blocks until every queued job dispatched by any task has finished.
options.rationale: The scheduler’s repeated-event loop is not a join on all background queue work.
options.misconception: The scheduler’s repeated-event loop is not a join on all background queue work.
